## **Jensen Huang deixou o comando da Nvidia após 33 anos**

- Huang renunciou ao cargo de CEO na semana passada, encerrando trajetória de 33 anos à frente da empresa que fundou;
- A saída aconteceu menos de uma semana depois de o executivo admitir um relacionamento extraconjugal. Reportagens também apontaram um suposto envolvimento com Alice Huang, que trabalhou para uma cliente da Nvidia e é suspeita de manter contatos com a inteligência chinesa, além de funcionários da própria companhia;
- No fim de semana, o _Financial Times_ informou que Jensen Huang teria conversado com aliados sobre a possibilidade de retornar ao comando da Nvidia;
- Brad Gerstner, fundador da Altimeter Capital, afirmou à _CNBC_ nesta segunda-feira que Huang não discutiu uma eventual volta com ele. Um representante do executivo também se recusou a comentar as especulações no domingo.

Uma petição online pela reinstalação de Huang já reuniu 180 mil assinaturas e recebeu apoio de figuras importantes do setor, incluindo Elon Musk, Garry Tan, CEO da Y Combinator, e Tim Sweeney, CEO da Epic Games.

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, também declarou nesta segunda-feira que está aberto à possibilidade de Huang reassumir o cargo.

Questionado sobre as preocupações envolvendo a segurança nacional estadunidense, Trump afirmou que o episódio não colocou o país em risco. “Isso não foi colocado em risco, e nosso país está agora mais forte do que nunca”, disse o presidente a jornalistas.

Na sexta-feira (13), um representante do conselho da Nvidia informou que a empresa estava em processo de seleção de uma consultoria especializada para conduzir a busca por um novo CEO.

# Robert Pattinson is Amazon’s first James Bond

Bond director Denis Villeneuve and Pattinson already worked together in the upcoming Dune: Part Three.

Bond director Denis Villeneuve and Pattinson already worked together in the upcoming Dune: Part Three.

byEmma Roth

Nov 16, 2026, 10:19 AM EST

Emma Rothis a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Robert Pattinson will take on the role of James Bond in Amazon MGM’s first film in the 007 franchise. The next _James Bond_ film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve using a script written by Steven Knight, while Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce.

The upcoming _James Bond_ film will be the first from Amazon, which snapped up the rights to the franchise through its acquisition of MGM Studios in 2021. Amazon later gained creative control over the spy series from Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson in 2025 after a years-long stalemate. There hasn’t been a new _James Bond_ film since Daniel Craig’s last installment as the spy in 2015’s _No Time to Die_.

Pattinson recently starred as _To Catch a Predator_ host Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller _Primetime_, and will appear in Villenueve’s _Dune: Part Three_ later this year. He also played Antinous in _The Odyssey_. Amazon MGM will now need to find actors to play a new Bond Lady, villain, along with an M and Q, as reported by _Deadline_.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson says in the press release. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

The AI-powered Ask Maps feature can suggest stops for your next trip, while providing real-time details about each location.

The AI-powered Ask Maps feature can suggest stops for your next trip, while providing real-time details about each location.

Emma Rothis a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days.

As an example, Google says you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping, or have it create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps will generate a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, while also showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map. You can share the itinerary with friends or family members, as well as export it to Google Docs on desktop.

Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.

Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter—even as an independent probe by Nvidia’s board investigates the conduct that led to a spectacular leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip company this week.

One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.

“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” they said. The efforts had Huang’s support, they added.

A public campaign to reinstate Huang has gathered steam over the weekend. Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney were among executives backing a public letter demanding that its board “Bring Jensen Back.”

Huang continues to command fierce loyalty from some employees, several of whom have gone public in calling for his return in the days since he resigned and have signed the open letter.

The effort to reinstate Huang is likely to face pushback from key policymakers in Washington, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday calling for a “dramatic shake-up” in leadership at the company after Huang’s departure.

Huang, who lacked the controlling shareholding of other founder-CEOs and was therefore unable to overule any board decision, also faces a board and a management team now led by interim chief executive Colette Kress that is aiming to steady the company ahead of quarterly results on Tuesday.

Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, has triggered deepening scrutiny of Nvidia’s compliance measures when selling its AI chips to customers in Asia who have potential links to China.

Even allies were unsure how to rehabilitate Huang’s reputation. “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense,” acknowledged one person involved in efforts to reinstate Huang.

The FT reported on Friday that Arm chief Rene Haas has been approached by Nvidia’s board as a potential successor. Nvidia’s board said no “formal” process had been initiated.

Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker—who are Nvidia shareholders—published an open letter to the board on Friday urging them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.”

The pair, both large investors in the company, cited “the extraordinary success of Jensen Huang’s leadership over a long period of time and given the massive uncertainty associated with recent events surrounding his departure” as reasons for clemency.

For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model.

For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he says, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. For some everyday applications, “80% might be good enough,” he says, but in areas such as supply chains or financial close, that level of accuracy is “a very terrible result.”

That foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing. Satinder Pal Singh, associate VP North America for SAP BAIP and SAP AI Strategy at Infosys, frames AI agents as “digital coworkers” and recommends evaluating potential use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. Companies should identify where an agent can move meaningful business metrics, determine whether their data and talent can support the use case, and then establish whether successful applications can be replicated. “A pilot that can't scale is just an experiment,” he says.

Scaling also brings governance into sharper focus. Clear policies, access controls, monitoring, and oversight are necessary to ensure agents remain trustworthy and aligned with business requirements. “The absence of governance doesn't speed up AI adoption,” Singh says. “It creates a risk backlog” that can ultimately force a more disruptive stop and audit.

Those considerations will become more important as AI agents take on more responsibilities as digital coworkers. Both executives see a future in which agentic systems coordinate work across applications, while customer-specific knowledge graphs and governed data become critical enterprise assets. For Singh, the longer-term opportunity is a shift from AI as a productivity tool to “AI as a decision-making partner,” helping leaders understand what is happening, anticipate what comes next, and determine how to respond.

_This episode of Business Lab is produced in partnership with Infosys._

**Full Transcript**

_Megan Tatum:_ From MIT Technology Review, I'm Megan Tatum, and this is Business Lab, the show that helps business leaders make sense of new technologies coming out of the lab and into the marketplace.

This episode is produced in partnership with Infosys.

Now, the development and democratization of AI tools has the potential to reconfigure how enterprises operate. But, at a time when applications are being scaled up from that initial phase of experimentation, we're still seeing senior leaders grapple with questions around AI's value, risk, and the complexity it adds. It's becoming clear that, unlike past ways of automation, AI requires a real mindset shift. Put simply, the technology can't simply be added into an enterprise's existing toolkit. It requires a complete reconfiguration of what's inside and how it's used.

Two words for you: conscious configuration.

My guests today are Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, and Satinder Pal Singh, Associate VP for North America, SAP Business AI Platform and SAP AI Strategy.

Welcome, Thorsten and Satinder.

_Thorsten Leiduck:_ Yeah, thank you for having us. Really a pleasure to be here with our valued partner, Infosys. Looking forward to the conversation.

_Satinder Pal Singh:_ Hi, Megan. Thanks for inviting for the conversation today. Looking forward to the discussion.

_Megan:_ Me too. Thank you both so much for being here. Thorsten, if I could start with you. We know that many senior leaders understand the transformative potential in AI, but they continue to struggle with aspects of its implementation. Many projects remain stuck at a pilot phase, for example. When you speak to clients, what are the biggest obstacles they face when it comes to integrating AI into their tech stack?

_Thorsten:_ Yeah. Megan, as you mentioned, AI is on the agenda of every client conversation today, but many customers are really struggling how to convert that interest into an operationalized model and to unlock the value of AI across the enterprise. And the reason is that too many programs start as isolated POCs on different AI technologies and in an inconsistent fragmented data foundation.

This creates a lot of duplication, inconsistent performance, and no clear path to scale. At the same time, leaders are highly concerned about security, observability, reliability of agents, and some ethical implications when those get deployed. This is also shown in some studies. For example, BCG has launched a report, which shows that 74% of the organizations are stuck in pilot mode with no plan to scale. And in an Anthropic survey, data said that 42% are really struggling with getting access to the data and the quality to really, basically, scale the entire AI capabilities across the organization.

The path forward is really to treat AI not just as a project, but more holistically, as an enterprise platform, one that really consistently connects an unified data layer with the process context of the applications, and then embed AI capabilities governed across the entire life cycle. And to make this real, we in SAP launched the SAP autonomous enterprise framework, so organizations can move from pilots to scaled outcomes.

_Megan:_ Yeah, really, to provide that support. And, Satinder, would you agree, why is it that we're seeing enterprises get a touch of almost AI paralysis here? What's the mindset shift that needs to happen and, perhaps, why is this something organizations need to be thinking about now, as well?

_Satinder:_ Absolutely, Megan. And, if anything, the picture sharpens when you look at, specifically, at agentic AI. Infosys and HFS research surveyed over 500 global 2,000 enterprises and found only 14% have successfully scaled AI. Eighty-six percent remain in early exploration, proof of concept, or fragmented pilot phases. For a technology at the top of every boardroom agenda for two years, that's a striking failure rate. And at the core of that 86% is what I would describe as AI as a department trap.

What happens is that an organization creates an AI team or a center of excellence and walls it off from business. That team builds technically excellent pilots the business doesn't recognize itself in, and you end up with AI solutions searching for problems, rather than the other way around. Mindset shift is clear. Move from treating AI as a technology initiative to treating it as an operating model transformation. AI stops being something IT does for business and starts being something the whole organization does together. Every function, every workflow, embedded from the start.

And what makes this a now problem? Early movers are building an advantage. You cannot close by buying the same platform later. Eighteen months of agent behavior data, calibrated knowledge graph, workforce that has genuinely internalized AI, that is a structural advantage that compounds. Infosys Knowledge Institute AI Maturity Index shows that only 8% of the companies qualify as AI native today, yet they achieve four times the revenue contribution from the AI versus laggards. If you're not building AI today, you're not standing still, you're falling behind at an accelerating rate.

_Megan:_ Right. There's a real polarization there, isn't there, between the front-runners and the laggards, as you say. As we shift from pilot to scaled-up applications, perhaps the first step is evaluating when AI is the right tool. AI has quickly become the default solution within many enterprises. Is there a tendency to use it as a bit of a blunt instrument, nowadays, Thorsten? At the outset, how can senior leaders better evaluate what use cases are worthy of their time and investment, in order to strip out some of that later complexity?

_Thorsten:_ Yeah, I think, Megan, what everybody needs to be aware is adopting and rolling out AI across an organization is as much a change management journey as it's a technology rollout.

Now, when you have this in mind, it makes absolutely sense to put AI in front as many teams as possible, because you want to build formality, and spark ideas, and also people should see the benefit of AI in an organization. When you think about travel assistance, meeting summaries via Copilot, or AI-enabled workflows, increase the productivity, everybody feels this in their real job, in their real daily business. And, obviously, this creates creativity and also provides the organization from a bottom-up perspective with some innovation scale.

Now, however, as majority grows, the conversation, and this is also what we discuss with many of the leaders, and our clients, shifts more to economics and governance. Things like token costs, model performance, security, and accountability become much more relevant. And when you then take the approach and think about AI agents as digital workers that execute specific tasks within a business process, then this means, from an AI perspective, not every task justifies nation.

In some cases, human effort remains more economical or effective. The smart approach, and that's what we really recommend to our clients, is to start with a defined, maybe small set of high-value use cases with defined success metrics upfront. So, for example, such as cycle time reduction, accuracy gains, or cost of per transaction, or top line improvement, and then scale what works. Those use cases can be tied to a line of business domains or industry scenarios.

And then, what we are doing from an SAP perspective, together with Infosys, we really help customers to be successful. We provide, as part of our autonomous suite, the according domain assistance, which really run business processes end-to-end and which deliver find ROIs for single end-to-end business process steps.

And then, last but not least, in many scenarios, I think, which has been very common pattern in particular around large industry AI use cases, is a joint approach, and we do this with partners like Infosys, but also customers around forward deployed engineering, so that you really define very closely the AI-specific use case with the defined outcomes together with the customer, and deliver this as the initial projects. And then, ideally, scale this to other customers and take it back like a best practice, which can be rolled out to other organizations, as well.

_Megan:_ Right. It's been really clear, isn't it, on what you're looking to achieve and what's worth your time, as I say. And what would your advice, Satinder, be here, on refining an AI strategy to ensure organizations can focus on those areas, where AI can deliver the highest returns?

_Satinder:_ Sure, Megan. I think Thorsten's framing of AI agents as digital coworkers forces a precision that agentic AI strategy language often lacks. When you ask which digital coworkers do we need and where do they deliver the most value, the answer starts to become clearer right from the first step. At Infosys, through our Topaz AI-first framework, we push clients through the three lenses simultaneously.

The first one is impact. Where does deploying an agent move the numbers that matter? Revenue, cost, working capital risk. We have built a library of over 300 enterprise use cases across industries, so we never begin from a blank page. The second is feasibility. Given your data foundation platform and talent today, which high-impact use cases can you actually execute? Feasibility determines your sequence. The high-impact use case on a broken data foundation is not viable. When the foundation is right, the results are dramatic. One Infosys engagement cut complex SAP-specification documents from 86 person hours to 6, a 92% reduction.

Third is scalability. Once you have proven a use case with clear ROI metrics, cycle time reduction, accuracy gains, cost per transaction, what's the architecture that lets you replicate it? A pilot that can't scale is just an experiment. My practical advice: treat your AI portfolio like an investment portfolio, quick wins that fund the program, medium-term bets, one or two bold, long-term positions that balance keep stakeholders engaged at every stage and not just in year three.

_Megan:_ That's such a useful framework for people to use there. And given the urgency here, Thorsten, how can organizations approach and manage AI in a more structured, efficient way? To start with, what are the fundamentals that some organizations perhaps miss at the moment? I know Infosys and SAP talk about platform and data, then AI, for example.

_Thorsten:_ Yeah, Megan, I think the fundamental, which many organizations are overlooking, is data and the data is a foundation for AI. Because, at the end, without the data structures and the ability to access the right information at the right time and basically bringing different kind of structured, unstructured data sources together, in a meaningful governed and semantic way, there will be no successful AI. AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation. And I think this is often overlooked, and that's why I said when you start POCs in different organization, or different parts of the organization with different technologies, it's very hard to establish an end-to-end consistent model on the data side, as well as on the AI side.

Os pesquisadores do Instituto Avançado de Ciência e Tecnologia da Coreia (KAIST) desenvolveram uma inteligência artificial que consegue **identificar palavras a partir dos movimentos dos lábios em vídeos sem áudio**. Batizado de DLLM-VSR, o sistema alcançou um novo recorde de precisão em testes de leitura labial por IA. A tecnologia ainda está em fase de desenvolvimento e não chegou ao público ou ao mercado.

Continua após a publicidade

O principal desafio desse tipo de ferramenta é **diferenciar palavras que produzem movimentos labiais muito parecidos**. É o caso das consoantes “p”, “b” e “m”, que podem ter aparências praticamente idênticas durante a fala. Para lidar com essa limitação, o DLLM-VSR utiliza um modelo de linguagem baseado em difusão (DLLM), que adota uma abordagem diferente das IAs tradicionais.

Os sistemas convencionais interpretam as palavras em sequência, da esquerda para a direita, o que pode influenciar o que vem depois. O DLLM-VSR segue outro caminho: identifica primeiro os termos sobre os quais tem maior confiança e usa essas palavras como referência para preencher as lacunas com informações **das partes anteriores e posteriores da frase**. O sistema também estima diferentes comprimentos possíveis para a frase com base na duração do vídeo, gera uma transcrição para cada opção e seleciona a versão mais plausível.

Nos testes, o DLLM-VSR registrou **uma taxa de erro de palavras (WER) de 19,4% no benchmark LRS3**, com treinamento baseado em 433 horas de vídeos rotulados. O resultado representa o melhor desempenho registrado entre os métodos treinados com o mesmo conjunto de dados. A métrica contabiliza palavras reconhecidas incorretamente, omitidas ou adicionadas durante a transcrição, mas não representa a porcentagem de conversas completas compreendidas corretamente.

A leitura labial automatizada pode abrir caminho para novos **recursos de acessibilidade** destinados a pessoas surdas ou com deficiência auditiva. Com a tecnologia, dispositivos poderiam converter conversas em texto a partir de imagens, mesmo quando não há gravação de áudio.

A ferramenta também pode ser útil em **ambientes industriais e situações cotidianas** com muito ruído, como restaurantes barulhentos ou locais com música alta, nos quais a comunicação por voz fica prejudicada.

# Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: the industry will be ‘fine’

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the AI industry will be “fine” without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the helm, even as he acknowledged the special role Huang has played in the AI boom.

Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement.

Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom.

Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return.

When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the company, Altman said: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.”

He expressed empathy for Huang’s situation, citing his own ousting from OpenAI in 2023 after board members accused him of withholding information.

“It’s hard to imagine what the AI revolution without Jensen and the company he has built,” Altman said, adding that he sees Huang as a hero, and that “heroes have flaws.”

OpenAI and Nvidia have had a close relationship for the last decade, one that has evolved from a simple chip supplier-customer relationship into a potentially circular financing arrangement, in which Nvidia’s money helps fund purchases of its own chips. Most recently, Nvidia agreed to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion backing OpenAI’s Ohio data center project. A **Galaxy Fit 3** está com um preço bem atraente para quem procura uma pulseira inteligente para acompanhar atividades físicas e monitorar dados de saúde. O modelo da Samsung pode ser encontrado por **R$ 179,10 no Pix**, uma ótima oportunidade para quem quer gastar pouco.

## Vale a pena comprar a Galaxy Fit 3?

Sim. A Galaxy Fit 3 é uma boa opção para quem quer acompanhar exercícios, monitorar o sono e visualizar notificações do celular sem precisar de um smartwatch mais caro.

Ela tem uma tela AMOLED de 1,6 polegada, com espaço suficiente para visualizar mensagens e informações de saúde. O modelo também oferece mais de 100 modos de exercícios, monitoramento de frequência cardíaca e oxigenação do sangue.

Outro destaque é a bateria, que pode durar até 13 dias, segundo a Samsung. A pulseira ainda tem resistência à água de 5 ATM e certificação IP68, o que permite seu uso em atividades aquáticas.

Continua após a publicidade

A principal limitação é a compatibilidade: **a Galaxy Fit 3 funciona apenas com celulares Android**. Portanto, quem tem iPhone precisa procurar outra opção.

## Galaxy Fit 3 vs Huawei Band 10 vs Xiaomi Smart Band 10

As três pulseiras oferecem recursos semelhantes para acompanhar atividades físicas e dados de saúde, mas existem diferenças importantes na tela, autonomia e compatibilidade.

Continua após a publicidade

| Característica | Galaxy Fit 3 | Huawei Band 10 | Xiaomi Smart Band 10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tela | AMOLED 1,6" | AMOLED 1,47" | AMOLED 1,72" |
| Bateria anunciada | Até 13 dias | Até 14 dias | Até 21 dias |
| Resistência à água | 5 ATM e IP68 | 5 ATM | 5 ATM |
| Compatibilidade | Android | Android e iOS | Android e iOS |
| Preço da oferta | R$ 179,10 | R$ 208,55 | R$ 319,90 |

A **Huawei Band 10** é a alternativa mais próxima da Samsung em preço. Ela custa R$ 208,55 no cartão e se destaca pelo design leve, monitoramento do sono e compatibilidade com iPhone.

Já a **Xiaomi Smart Band 10** oferece a maior tela das três e promete até 21 dias de bateria. No entanto, seu preço de R$ 319,90 no cartão é consideravelmente superior ao da Galaxy Fit 3.

## Qual pulseira inteligente vale mais a pena?

Continua após a publicidade

Pelos preços apresentados, a Galaxy Fit 3 é a escolha mais interessante para quem usa Android e quer economizar. A pulseira oferece um conjunto completo de funções básicas e custa menos que as concorrentes.

A Huawei Band 10 faz mais sentido para quem tem iPhone ou prefere um dispositivo mais compacto, especialmente pela diferença relativamente pequena de preço.

Por fim, a Xiaomi Smart Band 10 é indicada para quem prioriza uma tela maior e autonomia prolongada. Porém, vale considerar se essas vantagens justificam pagar bem mais.

### A Galaxy Fit 3 funciona com iPhone?

Continua após a publicidade

Não. A Galaxy Fit 3 não é compatível com iOS. Para quem usa iPhone, a Huawei Band 10 e a Xiaomi Smart Band 10 são alternativas compatíveis.

### A Galaxy Fit 3 tem GPS?

Não. A Galaxy Fit 3 não possui GPS integrado e depende do celular conectado para registrar a localização e o trajeto de exercícios ao ar livre.

### É possível responder mensagens pela Galaxy Fit 3?

Continua após a publicidade

Sim, a Galaxy Fit 3 permite responder notificações com mensagens predefinidas em celulares Android compatíveis. No entanto, não oferece teclado completo para digitar respostas livremente.

### A Galaxy Fit 3 pode ser usada para nadar?

Sim. A pulseira tem resistência de 5 ATM e certificação IP68, além de oferecer modos de exercícios aquáticos. Porém, não é indicada para mergulhos profundos ou esportes aquáticos de alta pressão.

Prefira o CT no Google Gabriel Furlan Batista/Canaltech Um vazamento revelou mudanças importantes no assistente virtual da Samsung . A Bixby 5.0 deve ter recursos de inteligência artificial para memorizar preferências, entender pedidos complexos e executar tarefas automaticamente. As novidades foram demonstradas pelo canal AppX, no YouTube, e detalhadas pelo site Android Authority.

A Bixby ganhará uma função chamada Memória para registrar informações pessoais e preferências, mantendo esses dados como referência em conversas futuras. O usuário poderá salvar informações com comandos, como “Lembre-se” e “Salve”, mas o assistente também será capaz de aprender com o histórico de chats.

O recurso ficará nas configurações avançadas do aplicativo e precisará de processamento na nuvem para oferecer respostas personalizadas. Caso o usuário escolha o processamento totalmente offline, as respostas poderão perder parte dessa personalização, já que a Bixby não conseguirá consultar as memórias salvas pela internet.

Vale ressaltar que essa função é diferente do aplicativo independente Samsung Memory, também identificado em vazamentos anteriores sobre a One UI 9.5. Enquanto o segundo tem uma proposta visual semelhante ao Pixel Screenshots, do Google, a memória integrada à Bixby serve especificamente para guardar o contexto pessoal entre conversas .

Receba as melhores ofertas de tecnologia Cupons e alertas de preço selecionados pela equipe do Canaltech, direto no seu WhatsApp. WhatsApp Continua após a publicidade A reformulação também transforma a Bixby em um agente de inteligência artificial que consegue dividir solicitações complexas em etapas e executá-las em segundo plano. No vídeo, o canal AppX usa o planejamento de uma viagem como exemplo hipotético do que o assistente poderá fazer no futuro, incluindo buscar hotéis, conferir opções disponíveis e ajudar no processo de reserva.

Já a aba Ações , acessível pelo menu lateral, funciona como uma central de tarefas agendadas. Com ela, será possível configurar buscas recorrentes por informações, como a cotação do dólar e o índice Nifty, em horários específicos. Antes de salvar uma rotina, o assistente pede a confirmação do usuário. As tarefas ficam registradas e podem ser pausadas, reativadas ou excluídas a qualquer momento.

A interface contará com mudanças para facilitar o envio de conteúdo durante as conversas . Uma nova barra flutuante chamada Ask Bixby terá um botão de adição (+) para anexar imagens da galeria, tirar fotos com a câmera ou selecionar arquivos do dispositivo. Na demonstração, o botão ainda apresenta funções mais básicas do que as encontradas no ChatGPT e no Gemini.

A tela inicial do assistente também vai ter uma organização diferente. No topo, a Bixby cumprimentará o usuário pelo nome e apresentará sugestões divididas em duas categorias: “Ações para experimentar” e “Coisas para perguntar”. A primeira traz ideias de tarefas, como resumir conversas com um contato em uma nota ou limpar o armazenamento do celular. A segunda apresenta sugestões de perguntas para fazer ao assistente.

A Samsung também prepara três novos widgets para a tela inicial dos Galaxy . Os atalhos incluem opções para abrir o microfone, digitar comandos, usar a câmera, anexar imagens da galeria e enviar arquivos. Os widgets atuais, incluindo os disponíveis na linha Galaxy S25, oferecem opções mais limitadas, concentradas em microfone, teclado e acesso ao Ask Bixby.

Os recursos foram identificados em um APK interno da Samsung , ainda não lançado oficialmente. Por isso, não há confirmação de que todas as novidades chegarão à versão final do assistente.

A expectativa é que a empresa apresente a One UI 9.5 junto à linha Galaxy S27 , no início de 2027. Caso o cronograma se confirme, a nova Bixby poderá estrear com a próxima geração de celulares da marca.

stories.title: Dona de GTA 6 critica OpenAI e Anthropic por “clones” de IA de jogos
stories.text: A Take-Two Interactive, a grande responsável por GTA 6 , criticou recentemente empresas como OpenAI e Anthropic por permitirem que ferramentas de inteligência artificial sejam usadas para copiar jogos existentes. Em entrevista ao IGN , o CEO Strauss Zelnick afirmou que as companhias precisam proteger a propriedade intelectual de desenvolvedores, especialmente diante do aumento de projetos que recriam jogos com IA generativa. A discussão sobre o tema é recorrente na indústria. O problema, inclusive, tem preocupado estúdios independentes, que relatam casos de jogos sendo reproduzidos em pouco tempo com o auxílio dessas tecnologias. Todas as empresas deveriam proteger suas propriedades, segundo CEO da Take-Two Foto: Rockstar/Divulgação Todas as empresas deveriam proteger suas propriedades, segundo CEO da Take-Two Ao comentar o uso de inteligência artificial para reproduzir jogos, Zelnick defendeu que empresas de tecnologia também devem respeitar os direitos autorais de terceiros. “Acho que todas as empresas deveriam proteger a propriedade intelectual, a sua própria e a de todos os outros”, afirmou o executivo ao IGN . Zelnick também criticou a postura de companhias que desenvolvem ferramentas de IA e, ao mesmo tempo, permitem que usuários utilizem seus serviços para reproduzir propriedades intelectuais. “Parece irônico, por um lado, desrespeitar a propriedade intelectual de outra pessoa e esperar que a sua esteja protegida”, acrescentou. A declaração acontece após a Anthropic implementar restrições no Claude para impedir que usuários recriem jogos específicos de outras empresas. A medida foi anunciada depois de desenvolvedores relatarem casos de reprodução de seus trabalhos com ferramentas de inteligência artificial. Segundo Addy Osmani, integrante da equipe técnica da Anthropic, utilizar o Claude para infringir direitos de propriedade intelectual viola as políticas da empresa. O executivo afirmou, porém, que jogos originais e projetos baseados em conceitos e recursos próprios continuam permitidos. Até o momento, a OpenAI não anunciou uma restrição equivalente. Questionado sobre a possibilidade de cópias de GTA 6 chegarem a plataformas não previstas pela Rockstar, Zelnick afirmou que a preocupação não está necessariamente relacionada a prejuízos financeiros, mas à preservação da experiência criativa idealizada pelo estúdio. O CEO também garantiu que a empresa acompanha os avanços tecnológicos e trabalha para proteger suas propriedades. CEO da Take-Two já afirmou que é “ridículo” achar que uma IA criará um jogo do nível de GTA 6 CEO da Take-Two já afirmou que é “ridículo” achar que uma IA criará um jogo do nível de GTA 6 Foto: Divulgação Essa não é a primeira vez que o executivo comenta sobre os limites da IA na indústria de games. Recentemente, o CEO da Take-Two classificou como “ridícula” a ideia de que ferramentas desse tipo possam criar jogos do porte de GTA 6 com apenas um comando . A declaração foi feita após a repercussão de tecnologias como o Project Genie, do Google, capaz de gerar experiências jogáveis a partir de instruções em texto. Para Zelnick, embora esses recursos possam auxiliar no desenvolvimento, eles não substituem o trabalho criativo necessário para produzir um grande jogo. “A ideia de que novas ferramentas permitiriam a um indivíduo apertar um botão e gerar um sucesso [...] é ridícula”, afirmou o executivo em março ao The Game Business . Segundo ele, a tecnologia, por si só, não garante o alcance global ou o impacto comercial de um lançamento. Quando GTA 6 será lançado? GTA 6 será lançado na próxima quinta (19). Foto: Rockstar/Divulgação Lembrando que GTA 6 será lançado em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. O título será disponibilizado exclusivamente nos consoles de atual geração inicialmente — mas é bastante provável que uma versão de PC também chegue no primeiro trimestre de 2027, segundo fortes rumores que circularam recentemente .
